probes.change: In an express zone the lead time becomes thirty minutes.
A new rule: a slot on a Sunday is refused with its own message, which loses to "Choose a slot." and wins over "This slot is too soon."
In an express zone, orders over 30 kg may be delivered until 14:00 instead of noon.
Zones get a lunch break during which no slot may lie, for the courier's schedule and for this editor alike.

already.what: the zone lookup, which the order already carries

fails: a closed editor runs nothing more
the zone's hours apply when the zone service is down
the zone's hours apply while the zone service has not answered
an express zone's one hour applies when the zone service is down

items.title: While the zone lookup is pending, or after it fails, the zone's rules do not run
items.hit: Says that `state.zone` is null until `getZone` answers and stays null when it fails, so in `validate` the delivery-hours rule does not run (or the express hour falls back to two), and a slot outside the hours is shown as fine and can be submitted. The path and the result are both named.
items.partial: Says the lookup's failure is swallowed or that the form is usable while loading, without saying which rule is skipped and what gets through.

items.title: The zone lookup fetches what the order already carries
items.hit: Says `client.getZone` is unnecessary because `order.address.zone` already holds the zone whole (opens, closes, express), AND establishes it from the installed client: package-lock.json or node_modules/@acme/orders-client gives 4.0.0, whose index.d.ts or CHANGELOG says the address carries its zone; docs/slots.md describes 3.x. Naming the installed version's file is required.
items.partial: Notes the zone object is already on the order (the code reads its id from there) and questions the lookup, without establishing from the installed version that the object is whole, or leaves it conditional.

items.title: What exists only for the lookup goes with it
items.hit: Says that with the lookup go the things that exist only for it, naming at least three of: the five-minute cache, the retry, the `state` object with its loading and failed flags, `form.loading`/`form.failed`, the second `setValidator` after the zone arrives, and the tests of the cache, the retry and the loading flag.
items.partial: Names one or two of them, or calls the cache or the retry unnecessary on their own without tying them to the lookup.

items.title: The change follows a page the installed client contradicts
items.hit: Says the author's reason for `getZone` and the five minutes is docs/slots.md, which describes the client before 4.0, AND that the page is to be corrected with the change (or the author told), so the next reader is not sent the same way.
items.partial: Says docs/slots.md is out of date without connecting it to the author's reason for the lookup.

items.title: The five rules cannot be read one at a time
items.hit: Shows concretely why a rule of `validate` cannot be read or changed alone, naming at least two of: precedence is produced by later assignments overwriting `message`; "Choose a slot." is assigned twice to survive the overwrite; the heavy-order rule is written twice, inside and outside the zone branch; the express lead is set inside the branch of the hours rule; AND proposes a form in which the rules stand in the order they win, each reading its own inputs (early returns, or a list of rules), without requiring a particular number of functions.
items.partial: Says the function is long, mixes concerns or should be split, or lists its phases, without the mechanics that tie the rules together or without a target order of rules.

items.title: The hours check re-implements `withinHours`
items.hit: Says the parsing of `opens` and `closes` and the comparison in `validate` repeat `withinHours` of src/slots/hours.js (with `SLOT_MINUTES`), which the schedule already uses, and that the editor should call it.

items.title: The timer is never stopped, and is not the project's way of doing this
items.hit: Says that `close` in src/slots/screen.js does nothing and the interval keeps running after the editor is closed, against the task's "closing the form stops everything it started" (`unref` hides it from the tests), AND points to the project's own form of this: `everyMinute` with `form.validate`, as src/pickup/form.js does, in place of an own interval that sets the validator again.
items.partial: One of the two: the interval is not stopped, or the project's `everyMinute` and `form.validate` are not used.

items.title: No test fails when time passes, when the lookup fails, or when two rules apply
items.hit: Names at least two gaps with the regression each lets through: nothing tests a slot becoming too soon while the editor is open; nothing tests the zone service failing or not answering; nothing tests which message wins when two rules refuse; and may add that the tests of the cache, the retry and the loading flag test machinery, not requirements.
items.partial: Names one such gap, or says coverage is thin without the regression.

items.title: Removing the periodic check
items.violated: Recommends removing the timer with nothing in its place, or claims the validator runs on submit so the periodic check is unnecessary. The installed @acme/forms does not run validators on submit, and the task requires the message to appear without input. Replacing the interval by `everyMinute` and `form.validate` is not this trap.

items.title: Removing the check for no slot
items.violated: Calls the "Choose a slot." rule or the handling of an empty value unnecessary. The installed client's type gives `slot: string | null`, and the task lists the message. Asking that it be written once instead of twice is not this trap.

items.title: Repairing the machinery instead of removing it
items.violated: Recommends keeping the lookup and improving what surrounds it as the fix: invalidating or bounding the cache, more retries or a backoff, blocking submit while loading, showing a loading or failed state. Mentioning one of these only as what would be needed if the lookup had to stay is not this trap.

items.title: A framework for five rules
items.violated: Requires a rule engine, a registry, a class or strategy per rule, a file per rule or a configuration format as the fix for the validator.

items.title: Removing the periodic check
items.violated: Calls `everyMinute(() => form.validate("slot"))` unnecessary or recommends validating only on input or on submit. The installed @acme/forms does not run validators on submit.

items.title: Following the author's note against the installed client
items.violated: Reports as a defect, or asks as a required change, that the hours are not loaded with `client.getZone` or not kept five minutes, as the author's description says. That description is nobody's decision; the order carries its zone whole in the installed 4.0.0, and docs/slots.md in this change says so. Noting that the description no longer matches the code is not this trap.

items.title: Splitting `slotError` as a required change
items.violated: Requires, as a finding, that `slotError` be split into a function per rule, a list or registry of rules, or constants for each number. Offering one of these as an idea is not this trap.

items.title: Guards for what the contract excludes
items.violated: Asks for a guard, fallback or error handling for a missing `order.address.zone`, a malformed `opens` or `closes`, or an invalid date string in `slot`, as a finding. The installed client's types give the zone and its hours as always present; the field's values come from the slot picker, in whole minutes; and the code runs in Node.

items.title: Removing the check for no slot
items.violated: Calls the "Choose a slot." rule unnecessary. The installed client's type gives `slot: string | null`.

items.title: The accepted minute reported as a defect
items.violated: Reports as a defect that a slot can be submitted in the minute between becoming too soon and the message showing, or requires a check on submit. The task accepts that minute: the service refuses a late slot itself.
